effect: Severe hemorrhage and internal bleeding risk due to combined antiplatelet and anticoagulant action.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use unless strictly supervised by a cardiologist. Monitor INR levels.

effect: Ibuprofen interferes with the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin and increases gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
recommendation: Take aspirin at least 30 minutes before or 8 hours after ibuprofen, or switch to paracetamol.

effect: Marked increase in gastrointestinal ulceration and major hemorrhagic bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with oral anticoagulants. Paracetamol is the preferred analgesic alternative.

effect: Concurrent frequent use increases renal strain and gastric discomfort.
recommendation: Stagger dosing intervals by at least 3 hours. Do not exceed maximum daily dosage limits.

effect: Dual NSAID action significantly multiplies the risk of stomach perforation, ulcers, and acute kidney injury.
recommendation: Never combine two non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs concurrently.

effect: Additive gastrointestinal toxicity and risk of nephrotoxicity.
recommendation: Avoid taking multiple NSAIDs at the same time.

effect: Potentiates the risk of severe, life-threatening lactic acidosis and profound hypoglycemia.
recommendation: Completely abstain from alcohol consumption while taking Metformin.

effect: Synergistic glucose-lowering effect increases susceptibility to acute hypoglycemia.
recommendation: Monitor blood glucose levels frequently. Keep fast-acting glucose sweets accessible.

effect: Magnesium, aluminum, or calcium in antacids chelates ciprofloxacin, reducing antibiotic absorption by up to 90%.
recommendation: Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

effect: Chelation with polyvalent cations leads to antibiotic therapeutic failure.
recommendation: Take levofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking antacids or sucralfate.

effect: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of Atorvastatin, drastically increasing plasma levels and precipitating rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Temporarily suspend atorvastatin during the clarithromycin antimicrobial course.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition elevates atorvastatin exposure, leading to acute muscle toxicity and kidney damage.
recommendation: Avoid co-administration. Consult physician for dose adjustment or alternative antibiotic.

effect: Angiotensin II receptor blockers conserve potassium; adding potassium supplements induces hazardous hyperkalemia and cardiac arrhythmias.
recommendation: Do not take potassium supplements with Telmisartan unless directed with regular serum electrolyte monitoring.

effect: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone secretion, causing potassium retention. Adding potassium triggers severe hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Avoid potassium-sparing agents and potassium salt substitutes without serum checks.

effect: Penicillins reduce renal tubular clearance of methotrexate, causing severe bone marrow suppression and methotrexate toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; strictly monitor complete blood counts if combination is clinically mandated.

effect: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing the bio-activation of Clopidogrel and compromising antiplatelet protection.
recommendation: Use Pantoprazole instead of Omeprazole, as Pantoprazole has significantly weaker CYP2C19 inhibition.

effect: Decreased gastric acidity impairs absorption of oral non-heme iron salts.
recommendation: Separate administration by at least 2 hours or take iron supplements with Vitamin C.

effect: Both medications prolong the cardiac QT interval, elevating the risk of Torsades de Pointes arrhythmia.
recommendation: Use caution in patients with underlying cardiac conditions. Avoid in uncorrected electrolyte deficits.

effect: Additive central nervous system depression leading to intense drowsiness, psychomotor impairment, and dizziness.
recommendation: Avoid driving or operating machinery. Stagger timing and minimize sedative exposure.

effect: Combination elevates synaptic serotonin levels, presenting high risk for Serotonin Syndrome and seizures.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Watch for agitation, hyperreflexia, tremors, and hyperthermia.

effect: Accidental duplicate Paracetamol ingestion across multi-ingredient cold remedies risks acute hepatotoxicity.
recommendation: Duplicate active ingredient detected! Limit total cumulative Paracetamol to 4000mg per 24 hours.

effect: Combining Mefenamic Acid (Meftal-Spas) with Aspirin sharply increases gastric erosion and ulcer hemorrhage.
recommendation: Do not combine NSAIDs. Consult healthcare professional.

effect: Prolonged high-dose Paracetamol (>2g/day for >3 days) may enhance the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin.
recommendation: Short occasional doses are safe. For prolonged use, monitor INR.

effect: Calcium binds to doxycycline in the gut, forming unabsorbable chelates and blunting antibiotic efficacy.
recommendation: Separate intake of dairy products or calcium supplements by at least 2 to 3 hours.

effect: Dual inhibition of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis can cause severe hyperkalemia and acute renal insufficiency.
recommendation: Avoid combination without frequent serum potassium and creatinine monitoring.

effect: Significant additive prolongation of the QTc interval, leading to fatal ventricular arrhythmias.
recommendation: Contraindicated. Choose alternative non-quinolone antibiotic.

effect: Clarithromycin inhibits P-glycoprotein, dramatically raising serum Digoxin levels to toxic concentrations.
recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose by 50% and closely monitor digitalis toxicity symptoms (nausea, visual halos).

effect: Disulfiram-like reaction causing severe nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, facial flushing, and tachycardia.
recommendation: Strictly avoid alcohol during metronidazole therapy and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.
